'''André Lee Roberson''' (born December 4, 1991) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[BC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]] of the [[VTB United League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado Buffaloes]]. As a junior in 2013, Roberson earned first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] honors in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]] for the second time and was also named the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Defensive Player of the Year|Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Year]]. He was selected in the first round of the [[2013 NBA draft]] with the 26th overall pick by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], but was acquired by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in a draft night trade. Roberson was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] in 2017.

==High school career==
Roberson attended [[Karen Wagner High School]] on the outskirts of [[San Antonio]]. During his senior year, Roberson averaged 15 points, 12 rebounds, and 1.7 blocked shots per game.<ref name="BIO" /> Considered a three-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], he was listed as the No. 62 power forward in the nation in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/100929/andre-roberson|title=Andre Roberson Recruiting Profile|work=ESPN.com|access-date=July 12, 2013}}</ref>

==College career==
Roberson played for the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado Buffaloes]] under coach [[Tad Boyle]]. In his three seasons at CU, Roberson was one of the country's top rebounders, finishing third in the country in [[2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2011–12]] and second in [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13]]. He led the Buffaloes to the NCAA Tournament both years.<ref name=BIO>{{cite web | title = #21 André Roberson | work = CUBuffs.com | url = http://www.cubuffs.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=600&ATCLID=204970260 | access-date = May 4, 2013}}</ref>

As a junior in 2012–13, Roberson averaged 10.9 [[Points per game|points]] and 11.2 [[rebounds per game]]. He was named first-team [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] and the conference [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Defensive Player of the Year|Defensive Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web| title =CU Buffs' Andre Roberson named Pac-12 defensive player of the year | work = DenverPost.com | date =March 11, 2013 | url =http://www.denverpost.com/cu/ci_22768520/cu-buffs-andre-roberson-named-pac-12-defensive | access-date = May 4, 2013}}</ref> At the end of his junior season, Roberson announced that he was forgoing his remaining NCAA eligibility to enter the [[2013 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web| title =Andre Roberson entering NBA draft | work = ESPN.com | date =April 28, 2013 | url =https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2013/story/_/id/9221890/colorado-buffaloes-junior-andre-roberson-entering-nba-draft | access-date = May 4, 2013}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Oklahoma City Thunder (2013–2020)===
Roberson was selected with the 26th overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], but was later acquired by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on draft night.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/06/27/wolves-make-three-team-trade.ap/|title=Wolves trade 26th pick Roberson in three-team trade|work=NBA.com|date=June 27, 2013|access-date=December 3, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131214061809/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/06/27/wolves-make-three-team-trade.ap/|archive-date=December 14, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> On July 12, he signed with the Thunder after an impressive [[2013 NBA Summer League|Summer League]] performance.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/adams_roberson_130712|title=Thunder Signs Steven Adams and Andre Roberson|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 12, 2013|access-date=July 12, 2013}}</ref> During his rookie season, Roberson had multiple assignments with the [[Tulsa 66ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html|title=2013-14 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=July 4, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140703151241/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html|archive-date=2014-07-03|url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[File:LeBron James vs Andre Roberson.jpg|thumb|left|Roberson defends [[LeBron James]] in January 2015]]
In July 2014, Roberson re-joined the Thunder for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/basketballnews/release_summer_league_2014|title=Thunder Announces Summer League Roster|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 4, 2014|access-date=July 4, 2014}}</ref> On October 22, 2014, the Thunder exercised their third-year team option on Roberson's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_thunder_141022|title=Thunder Exercises Options on Adams, Roberson Jones and Lamb|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 22, 2014|access-date=November 16, 2014}}</ref> Earning the Thunder's starting [[shooting guard]] spot for the [[2014–15 Oklahoma City Thunder season|2014–15 season]], Roberson recorded his first career double-double (10 points, 12 rebounds) on December 18 against the [[Golden State Warriors]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/roberan03/gamelog/2015/|title=Andre Roberson 2014-15 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 9, 2015}}</ref> and scored a then career-high 12 points on February 9 against the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/recap_nuggets_150209|title=Thunder at Denver Nuggets Game Recap – Feb. 9, 2015|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 9, 2015|access-date=February 9, 2015}}</ref>

On October 23, 2015, the Thunder exercised their fourth-year team option on Roberson's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/pressrelease_options_exercised_151023|title=Thunder Exercises Options on Adams, Roberson and McGary|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 23, 2015|access-date=October 23, 2015}}</ref> He retained the starting shooting guard spot in [[2015–16 Oklahoma City Thunder season|2015–16]], and on December 23, Roberson scored a then career-high 15 points in a 120–85 victory over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/recap_lakers_151223|title=Thunder at Los Angeles Lakers Game Recap – Dec. 23, 2015|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=December 23, 2015|access-date=January 25, 2016}}</ref> On January 25, 2016, he was ruled out for three weeks with a right knee sprain.<ref>{{cite web|last=Slater|first=Anthony|url=http://newsok.com/article/5474649|title=OKC Thunder: Andre Roberson to miss at least three weeks with knee sprain|work=NewsOK.com|date=January 25, 2016|access-date=January 25, 2016}}</ref> Roberson returned to action on February 24 after missing 10 games.<ref>{{cite web|last=Mayberry|first=Darnell|url=http://newsok.com/article/5480921|title=Oklahoma City Thunder: Andre Roberson returning to the starting lineup|work=NewsOK.com|date=February 24, 2016|access-date=February 25, 2016}}</ref> In Game 4 of the [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]] Finals, he scored a career-high 17 points and grabbed 12 rebounds, as the Thunder defeated the Golden State Warriors 118–94 to take a 3–1 lead in the series.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160524/GSWOKC/gameinfo.html|title=Westbrook, Thunder put Warriors on brink of elimination|work=NBA.com|date=May 24, 2016|access-date=May 24, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160524203410/http://www.nba.com/games/20160524/GSWOKC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=May 24, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> However, the Thunder went on to lose the series in seven games.

Roberson was moved to the starting [[small forward]] spot for the [[2016–17 Oklahoma City Thunder season|2016–17 season]] due to the loss of [[Kevin Durant]] and the acquisition of [[Victor Oladipo]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Heim|first=Tony|url=http://thunderousintentions.com/2016/09/14/andre-roberson-small-forward/|title=Andre Roberson: Is he ready to play small forward this season?|work=thunderousintentions.com|date=September 14, 2016|access-date=February 25, 2017|archive-date=February 25, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170225205540/https://thunderousintentions.com/2016/09/14/andre-roberson-small-forward/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 24, 2017, Roberson set a new career high with 19 points in a 110–93 victory over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900267|title=Westbrook's triple-double leads Thunder past Lakers, 110-93|work=ESPN.com|date=February 24, 2017|access-date=February 25, 2017}}</ref> At the season's end, he was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/roberson-defense-second-team-170626|title=Andre Roberson Named to 2016-17 NBA All-Defensive Second Team|work=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2017|access-date=June 27, 2017}}</ref>[[File:Andre Roberson 2017.jpg|thumb|right|Roberson in 2017]]

On July 14, 2017, Roberson re-signed with the Thunder to a three-year, $30 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/roberson-extension-170714|title=Thunder Signs Andre Roberson to Multi-Year Contract Extension|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2017|access-date=July 14, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://newsok.com/article/5556365|title=Andre Roberson: OKC 'the place I wanted to be'|work=NewsOK.com|date=July 14, 2017|access-date=July 14, 2017}}</ref> After missing eight games in January 2018 with left patellar tendinitis,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975406|title=Anthony, Adams lead Thunder past Lakers 114-90|work=ESPN.com|date=January 17, 2018|access-date=January 20, 2018}}</ref> he ruptured his left patellar tendon on January 27 against the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/01/27/oklahoma-city-guard-andre-roberson-injured-leaves-court-gurney#/|title=Report: Thunder guard Andre Roberson ruptures patellar tendon against Pistons|work=NBA.com|date=January 27, 2018|access-date=January 28, 2018}}</ref> Roberson underwent surgery the following day and was subsequently ruled out for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/roberson-procedure-180128|title=Roberson Undergoes Successful Procedure|work=NBA.com|date=January 28, 2018|access-date=January 28, 2018}}</ref>

On October 4, 2018, Roberson was ruled out for an additional two months after undergoing a procedure following a setback during his rehab from left knee surgery.<ref>{{cite web|last=Young|first=Royce|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/24896434/thunder-andre-roberson-miss-two-more-months-knee-setback|title=Thunder's Andre Roberson to miss two more months after knee setback|work=ESPN.com|date=October 4, 2018|access-date=October 4, 2018}}</ref> In late November, he experienced discomfort after landing from a jump, and an MRI revealed that he had suffered a small avulsion fracture in his knee. Roberson was subsequently ruled out for at least another six weeks.<ref>{{cite web|last=Young|first=Royce|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/25419118/thunder-andre-roberson-knee-setback-miss-six-more-weeks|title=Thunder's Andre Roberson has knee setback, will miss six more weeks|work=ESPN.com|date=November 30, 2018|access-date=November 30, 2018}}</ref>

On August 1, 2020, Roberson played his first NBA game in over two years, logging five minutes in a 110–94 victory over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=GILGEOUS-ALEXANDER SCORES 19 TO HELP THUNDER TOP JAZZ 110-94 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021901240 |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2021)===
On February 16, 2021, Roberson signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Andre Roberson |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/02/16/brooklyn-nets-sign-andre-roberson |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 16, 2021 |date=February 16, 2021}}</ref> He played two games for the Nets before being waived on February 23.<ref>{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Waive Three Players |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/brooklyn-nets-waive-three-players |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 24, 2021 |date=February 23, 2021}}</ref> Three days later, Roberson signed a 10-day contract with the Nets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Andre Roberson and Iman Shumpert to 10-day Contracts |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/02/26/brooklyn-nets-sign-andre-roberson-and-iman-shumpert-10-day-contracts |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 27, 2021 |date=February 26, 2021}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Blue (2023)===
On February 1, 2023, Roberson signed with the [[Oklahoma City Blue]], the Thunder's [[NBA G League|G League]] affiliate.<ref>{{Cite web |title=OKC BLUE on Twitter: "The Oklahoma City Blue has acquired guard/forward Andre Roberson, the team announced today." |url=https://twitter.com/okcblue/status/1620935046164250625 |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=Twitter}}</ref>

===Cholet Basket (2024)===
On September 5, 2024, Roberson signed with [[Cholet Basket]] of [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cholet-basket-officially-signs-andre-roberson/|title=Cholet Basket officially signs Andre Roberson|work=Sportando |date=September 5, 2024|language=En|access-date=September 5, 2024 |last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }}</ref>

===ASVEL Lyon-Villeurbanne (2024–2025)===
[[File:André Roberson 21 ASVEL Euroleague 20250313 (6).jpg|thumb|right|Roberson with [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL Lyon-Villeurbanne]] in 2025]]
On November 8, 2024, Roberson signed with [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL Lyon-Villeurbanne]] of the French [[LNB Élite]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/asvel-officially-signs-andre-roberson/|title=ASVEL officially signs Andre Roberson
|work=Sportando
|date=November 8, 2024|language=En|access-date=November 8, 2024
|last1=Maggi
|first1=Alessandro
}}</ref>

===Zenit St. Petersburg (2025–present)===
On July 31, 2025, Roberson signed with [[Zenit Saint Petersburg]] of the [[VTB United League]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Andre Roberson is in Zenit|url=https://vtb-league.com/en/news/andre-roberson-is-in-zenit/|access-date=October 1, 2025|website=vtb-league.com|language=en}}</ref> He averaged 9.2 points, 6.8 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.2 steals per game. Roberson re-signed with the team on July 11, 2026.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zenit keeps Roberson for another season |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Russia/news/1008817/Zenit-keeps-Roberson-for-another-season |website=Eurobasket |access-date=July 13, 2026 |date=July 11, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Roberson comes from a family of athletes. Both of his parents were All-Americans in their respective sports during college at [[New Mexico State University|New Mexico State]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.texasredzonereport.com/2015/12/the-roberson-pedigree-comes-to-texas-state/|title=The Roberson Pedigree comes to Texas State {{!}} Texas Redzone Report|last=Ciardello|first=Keff|website=www.texasredzonereport.com|access-date=2016-08-25|archive-date=August 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160826233954/http://www.texasredzonereport.com/2015/12/the-roberson-pedigree-comes-to-texas-state/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Roberson has six siblings. All the Roberson children are current or former [[NCAA Division I]] athletes.<ref name=":0" />

In August 2025, Roberson married former [[Old Dominion University]] women's basketball player and television host, [[Rachel Annamarie DeMita]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Instagram |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DJFeAX2Snnq/?img_index=1 |access-date=2025-05-09 |website=www.instagram.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Rachel DeMita - Women's Basketball 2008-09 |url=https://odusports.com/sports/womens-basketball/roster/player/rachel-demita |access-date=2025-05-09 |website=Old Dominion Athletics |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web
